claims.statement: Coverage A is line-specific: DP-3 2012-11 and 2026-01 require 80% of dwelling replacement cost for replacement-cost settlement, DP-3 2020-08 requires 90%, the cited HO-3 and HO-5 editions require 80%, HO-6 covers unit-owner building property rather than the entire condominium building, and HO-4 2013-07/2021-10 expressly provide no Coverage A building insurance.

Coverage B limits vary by edition: the cited DP-3 2012-11, DP-3 2020-08, and HO-3/HO-5 editions state 10% of Coverage A, DP-3 2026-01 states 15%, and HO 04 48 (2026-06) replaces the HO-3 2024-03 base 10% limit with 20%; the supplied HO-4 and HO-6 Coverage B sections do not state a Coverage A-based percentage.

The cited HO-3 and HO-5 editions state Coverage C at 50% of Coverage A, while the supplied DP-3 2012-11, 2020-08, and 2026-01 forms state a 0% Coverage C limit; the supplied HO-4 and HO-6 Coverage C sections provide applicable limits and special limits without stating a Coverage C percentage in the cited sections.

Coverage D limits and architecture differ materially: the cited HO-3/HO-5 editions use 20% of Coverage A, HO-6 uses 50%, HO-4 2013-07 states 30% and HO-4 2021-10 states 40% despite their no-Coverage-A provisions, and DP-3 changes from a 20% FRV limit in 2012-11 to a 25% FRV limit in 2020-08 and a 30% aggregate Coverage D limit in 2026-01.

Coverage D responds to loss of use caused by a covered physical loss that makes the residence or rented part unfit, pays necessary increased living expense or actual lost fair rental value reduced by noncontinuing expenses, generally requires mitigation and records, and generally ends when the property is fit or access is restored.

HO 04 20 (2016-08) acts on the HO-3 Coverage A limit by adding 25% after the base limit is exhausted, while preserving the base Coverage A property grant, valuation method, exclusions, limitations, personal-property limit, and loss-of-use limit.

HO 04 40 (2011-05) writes back to the HO-3 2011 Coverage B rental exclusion by covering a qualifying rental structure on the residence premises and landlord furnishings up to $5,000, while expressly not providing personal-property, liability, or loss-of-use coverage for the rental structure.

HO 04 48 (2026-06) replaces the HO-3 2024-03 base Coverage B limit of 10% of Coverage A with 20% of Coverage A, but preserves the other Coverage B property, exclusion, duty, and deductible rules unless the endorsement conflicts with them.

HO 17 33 (2014-04) changes the HO-6 2014-04 Coverage A grant to coverage for a risk of direct physical loss subject to the endorsement's exclusions and limitations and sets a $25,000 Coverage A limit, instead of the base form's stated $5,000 default limit.

Coverage C special limits are generally inside the parent Coverage C limit rather than additional insurance; examples include HO-3 2018 special limits and HO-5 2022 special limits for money, jewelry, firearms, watercraft, silverware, business property, and vehicle-installed electronics.

The base-form peril structure differs between HO-3 and HO-5: the cited HO-3 2018 Coverage C enumerates named perils, while HO-5 2022 grants direct physical loss unless excluded and then states exclusions and ensuing-loss rules.

HO-6 Coverage A is unit-owner property and includes improvements, fixtures, appliances, and certain common property only to the extent of the owner's interest or legal responsibility; it is not automatically coverage for the condominium association's entire building.
